Categories.value: Neermahal|Self-published work|Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation|2025 in Tripura|Taken with Canon EOS R50|Photographs by Kingshuk Mondal|Photographs of Neer Mahal by Kingshuk Mondal

ImageDescription.value: Neermahal, or Twijilikma Nuyung, is a former royal palace of the Tripura Kingdom, situated in the middle of Rudrasagar Lake. Built as a summer residence by Maharaja Bir Bikram Kishore Manikya Bahadur in 1930 (construction began in 1921), it is the largest water palace in India. The Maharaja commissioned the British company, Martin and Burns, to construct this unique palace, which took nine years and blends Hindu and Mughal architectural styles. It features balconies, towers, pavilions, and dome-shaped minars. The palace is divided into the Andar Mahal (for the royal family) and an eastern side with an open-air theatre. It has 24 rooms and is 53 kilometers from Agartala.
